StackType.issue: PowerStackType.Single, and this is the one unit in the on_stack family that goes the OTHER way: the sim does NOT override on_stack, so a second application adds. That happens to be what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236), so it is *more* faithful than the 15 units that override it to `pass` -- but it is still a gap, because C#'s AfterApplied fires only on a genuinely new power while the sim's __init__-time Minion grant (powers.py:1562-1564) likewise only runs on construction. Dormant: nothing reads Illusion's Amount, and the sim's stacking path (cmds.py:308-322) would not re-run __init__ anyway. Recorded so the inconsistency between this unit and its 15 siblings is visible.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath.issue: IllusionPower.cs:59-66 keeps the owner's BUFFS (including itself) through death and drops only non-ITemporaryPower Debuffs -- the source comment explains that Temporary powers are excluded so the temp powers THEY applied also go away. The sim has no `should_power_be_removed_on_death` hook (hooks.py defines none) and never removes powers on death at all, so the whole predicate is unreachable in the sim. **RE-DERIVED 2026-07-26 (review fix pass): the previous dormancy argument rested on a FALSE grep.** It said "`grep IllusionPower` outside powers.py finds no sim applier at all". There are two: `monsters/hive/the_obscura.py:38-39` (Parafright) and `monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py:34-35` (Eye with Teeth) both `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, IllusionPower, 1)` from __init__, mirroring Parafright.cs:35-39 and EyeWithTeeth.cs:30-34's AfterAddedToRoom. Both are ported summons of ported enemies (The Obscura is a Hive elite, Fogmog an Overgrowth normal). So the buff half stays dormant-by-agreement (the sim keeps everything, which is what this override asks for) and the DEBUFF half is **LIVE, not dormant**: the game clears a dying Illusion's Vulnerable/Weak/Frail and the sim carries them into the revived creature. EXECUTED: an Eye with Teeth given Vulnerable 3, hit for 99, then revived, comes back at 6/6 HP still holding `vulnerable` 3 in the sim; in the game Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath (Creature.cs:668-671) strips it, because VulnerablePower does not override ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath (default true, PowerModel.cs:637-640) and IllusionPower is the only ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath implementer in the whole game, returning true for any non-temporary Debuff. Bash/Vulnerable and Clothesline/Weak are ported basic-pool Ironclad content, so a revived Illusion is straightforwardly weaker in the game than in the sim. The engine-level half of this -- that the sim never strips ANY power on death -- is audits/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8b (added in the same fix pass); this entry owns IllusionPower's own predicate. ITemporaryPower has no sim analogue either (there is no `dark_shackles`-style wrapper in the ported set that survives here), and no ported debuff on an Illusion is temporary, so the ITemporaryPower carve-out itself is inert. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterApplied.rationale: C# grants MinionPower 1 from AfterApplied unless the owner already has it (IllusionPower.cs:68-75, applier null, cardSource null); the sim does it in __init__ with the same `"minion" not in owner.powers` test (powers.py:1562-1564) and the same absent applier. The sim has no AfterApplied slot, and __init__ runs at exactly the point PowerCmd.apply creates the power (cmds.py:324-327) -- i.e. BEFORE hooks.on_power_applied rather than after, which is the only difference and is unobservable because no ported listener reacts to a Minion grant. Named per the main report's section 7 item 6: the mechanism is __init__-for-AfterApplied, and it would break for any AfterApplied body that needs the power to already be registered.

AfterDeath.issue: Same wrong-hook shape as AdaptablePower's, and not re-argued here: C# lets the death happen and retains the corpse; the sim prevents the death and floors the owner at 1 HP (cmds.py:112). Consequences (1) HP 1 vs 0 and (2) damage_pipeline gap G4's killing-blow-skip recomputation apply identically. The (3) Feed consequence does NOT apply here and it is worth saying why: IllusionPower auto-applies MinionPower, whose ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal() is false, so C# also refuses the fatal -- which is exactly what cards/feed.py:17-18's docstring claims, correctly for Illusion and incorrectly for Adaptable. The (4) Gremlin Horn consequence DOES apply: see power/adaptable's AfterDeath entry, and note both of this power's ported appliers are enemies, so `target.Side != Owner.Creature.Side` holds and the game pays out on every Illusion "death". Additionally absent: C#'s AfterDeath installs a synthetic REVIVE_MOVE MoveState whose FollowUpStateId is `FollowUpStateId ?? MoveStateMachine.StateLog.Last().Id` and whose MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning is true (IllusionPower.cs:83-88) -- the sim has no such splice, leaving the revive to the owner's own take_turn calling `revive()` (powers.py:1577-1581). **RE-DERIVED 2026-07-26 (review fix pass): the old dormancy reason for this clause -- "no sim applier exists" -- was FALSE (see this record's ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath entry; Parafright and Eye with Teeth both apply it).** It is dormant for a different and checkable reason: BOTH ported appliers have a single self-looping move state -- Parafright.cs:44-47 `SLAM_MOVE` with `moveState.FollowUpState = moveState`, EyeWithTeeth.cs:39-42 `DISTRACT_MOVE` likewise -- so `StateLog.Last().Id` is always that one state and "resume the logged move" cannot differ from "resume where the machine is", which is what the sim's take_turn does (monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py:48-56, monsters/hive/the_obscura.py). Neither applier sets FollowUpStateId, so it stays null on both. Named trigger: porting an IllusionPower applier with a multi-state move machine, or any caller that sets FollowUpStateId. Third-file citations, not hashed here. ONE MECHANISM, ONE VERDICT (binding rule 3): power/adaptable, power/illusion and power/steam_eruption all implement a C# AfterDeath body by returning False from `should_die` (powers.py:3365-3369, :1566-1570, :2016-2020), so all three run the sim's single death-PREVENTION branch (cmds.py:106-113) where C# runs the REAL-DEATH branch (CreatureCmd.cs:505-559). None of the three overrides ShouldDie, and all three bodies sit behind `!wasRemovalPrevented` (AdaptablePower.cs:34, IllusionPower.cs:79, SteamEruptionPower.cs:17) -- i.e. they are explicitly EXCLUDED from the branch the sim is executing. All three therefore carry `gap`; steam_eruption's `deliberate-divergence` was corrected to `gap` in the 2026-07-26 review fix pass. The canonical statement of the shared observable (the Gremlin Horn witness) is on power/adaptable's AfterDeath entry.

ShouldAllowHitting.issue: LIVE, and it upgrades a seam gap that was recorded as un-demonstrated. C#'s PowerCmd.Apply<T> refuses to apply anything to a creature `CanReceivePowers` says no to, and CanReceivePowers reuses Hook.ShouldAllowHitting -- which is exactly what this override's own doc comment says it is for ("This is so the ... doesn't receive POWERS while it is reviving"). The sim wires should_allow_hitting into DamageCmd.deal (cmds.py:51-52) but NOT into PowerCmd.apply, which has no such guard at all. That is `power_cmd` gap **G6**, whose text says "No concrete broken interaction is demonstrated (spot-checked callers apply powers only to already-resolved targets)". **That is now falsified. EXECUTED:** a TEST_SUBJECT_BOSS combat (the Test Subject starts with powers ['adaptable', 'enrage']), a lethal Strike, then Vulnerable 2 from the player -- the sim reports `is_reviving True`, `should_allow_hitting(ts) False`, and then still lands `Vulnerable(2)` on the reviving boss, where the game refuses the application outright. Control: a 10-damage Strike in the same window returns 0 HP lost, proving the predicate IS wired into the damage path and only the power path is missing it. Rule-6 co-occurrence: the Test Subject is the ported Act-3 Glory boss and applies this power to itself at combat start, Bash/Vulnerable is ported basic-pool Ironclad content, and the revive window is the remainder of the player's turn after the killing blow -- the ordinary flow of the fight, not a contrived state. The same override exists on IllusionPower and ReattachPower, so all three carry it. Verdict carried per rule 3; the seam record is not edited (half B does not own audits/seam/** or docs/audit/seams/**) -- reported in .superpowers/sdd/content-power-report-b.md section 2.3. Third-file citations, not hashed here. NOTE (2026-07-26 fix pass): this record's own appliers make the finding reachable without the Test Subject at all -- Parafright (monsters/hive/the_obscura.py:38-39) and Eye with Teeth (monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py:34-35) each open the same revive window on their own "death", and a Vulnerable landed on either during it is refused by the game and accepted by the sim.

guards.what: The prevention branch's HP contract: sim `hp = 1` vs C# leaving the creature at 0 and re-entering KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition
guards.issue: Part of the should_die-for-AfterDeath mechanism, carried as its own entry because it survives any fix that only re-slots the AfterDeath body. cmds.py:112 writes `target.hp = 1` and stops. C# does NOT heal the creature: CreatureCmd.cs:560-571 leaves it at 0 HP, fires Hook.AfterDeath(wasRemovalPrevented: true) and Hook.AfterPreventingDeath, and then, `if (creature.IsDead)`, RE-ENTERS `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition(creature, force, recursion + 1)` -- up to 10 times before throwing InvalidOperationException (:562-565). So in the game a preventer must actually raise the creature's HP (Fairy in a Bottle heals; these three do not, which is why they take C#'s DEATH branch and not this one), whereas the sim's single silent `hp = 1` makes any prevention permanent and models neither the re-entry nor the 10-deep bail-out. Two consequences beyond the 1-vs-0 HP that conformance asserts on directly: the sim cannot express a prevention that fails, and the sim's own steam_eruption HP restore only runs because this floor makes `target.is_dead` False at cmds.py:121 (damage_pipeline gap G4). Same verdict at all three sites per rule 3.

guards.what: The non-damage kill path: CreatureCmd.kill reproduces both arms but fires no on_damage_received
guards.issue: Part of the same mechanism, at the second of the sim's two death sites. `CreatureCmd.kill` (cmds.py:191-205) mirrors DamageCmd.deal's should_die / should_remove_from_combat_after_death / on_death fork and the same `target.hp = 1` prevention floor, but it is not a damage event, so it fires neither on_damage_received nor after_preventing_death. Consequences: (a) power/steam_eruption's HP restore (powers.py:2022-2033) lives on on_damage_received and therefore does not run here at all, leaving the Waterfall Giant at hp 1 instead of the 999999999 WaterfallGiant.cs:305 sets; (b) the preventer never learns the death was prevented. DORMANT for these three powers today -- the only ported non-damage kill of a steam_eruption owner is the giant's own `_explode` (monsters/underdocks/waterfall_giant.py:142-145), which runs AFTER `_about_to_blow` removed the power at :140, and nothing kills the Test Subject or an Illusion off the damage path. Named trigger: any ported non-damage kill reaching a creature that still holds one of these three powers -- SandpitPower._expire (powers.py:2610-2619) and TheGambitPower (powers.py:3816-3829) are the two ported callers of CreatureCmd.kill outside a monster's own move. Same verdict at all three sites per rule 3.
